facts.text: every custom option is a field on the exported `ZestCustomProps` interface passed as the `zest` prop; no custom prop is top-level on ZestButtonProps.
split mode is a plain `<div className={styles.splitButtonContainer}>` wrapping the main `<button>` plus `ZestDropdownMenu`; the wrapper has no role, tabindex or aria attributes.
the main button always carries `styles.button` (position:relative; overflow:hidden) and split mode adds `styles.splitButtonMain` (right radii 0, border-right none).
disabled/busy state is `isDisabled` (disabled || effectiveBusy || rage-click || anyDropdownItemBusy), applied as the real `disabled` attribute plus `styles.disabled`.
focus ring is `.button:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--zest-shadow-resting), var(--zest-focus-ring) }` (line 179); the ring is an outer box-shadow, so a clipping ancestor can cut it.
chevron mount streak is `.dropdownTrigger::before` (lines 572-586, 115deg, 1.3s, 0.4s delay) and is switched off under `prefers-reduced-motion` at lines 645-667.
`.splitButtonContainer` (line 495) is only `display:inline-flex; align-items:stretch` today — no position, overflow or border-radius; `--zest-radius-md` (8px) is the button corner radius.
menu content is inside `DropdownMenu.Portal` (line 85), so a clipping/positioned split wrapper does not clip the open menu.
`ZestGlobalConfig.defaultProps?: ZestCustomProps`, so any new ZestCustomProps field can also be supplied app-wide through the provider's generic defaultProps.
CSS Modules are mapped to identity-obj-proxy (jest.setup/jsdom), so class-name and DOM assertions work but computed styles/animations do not; existing tests parse CSS/config source text where needed.
custom options are fields on ZestCustomProps, merged by useZestConfig (provider defaultProps -> semantic defaults -> local zest), so a new `focusSheen` field needs no extra plumbing.
hasDropdown is `dropdownOptions && length > 0`; split mode renders `<div className={styles.splitButtonContainer}>` wrapping the main `<button>` plus ZestDropdownMenu.
button className already includes styles[buttonStyle], styles[variant], styles[size] and force-light/force-dark; effectiveTheme and variant/buttonStyle are available when rendering the split wrapper.
`.button` already has position:relative, overflow:hidden and border-radius:var(--zest-radius-md), so a `::after` streak on it is clipped to the rounded shape.
the focus ring is an outer box-shadow on `.button:focus-visible` (line 179), so a clipping ancestor/wrapper would cut it; the split wrapper must not use overflow:hidden.
`.splitButtonContainer` (line 495) is only display:inline-flex;align-items:stretch — it has no position, overflow or border-radius.
chevron mount streak is `.dropdownTrigger::before` + keyframes dropdownTriggerDiscoverySheen (115deg, 1.3s, 0.4s delay); suppress it with a wrapper class, no JS.
existing reduced-motion block (line 645) already sets `.dropdownTrigger::before { animation:none; content:none }`, so new streak rules can join that media query.
`color-mix(in srgb, ...)` is already used (toggleOn, line 785/847) with a static fallback, so colour-mix is an accepted pattern here.
there is no `::after` rule anywhere in the file today, so `.button::after` and `.splitButtonContainer::after` are free.
the chevron trigger is a `.button .dropdownTrigger` and the menu is inside DropdownMenu.Portal, so clipping/clipping-like wrapper changes cannot affect the open menu.
tests read Styles/ZestButton.module.css as text and assert on selector/source strings because CSS Modules map to identity-obj-proxy in jsdom.
`export * from "./ZestButton"` already re-exports ZestCustomProps, so adding an optional field needs no index.ts change and is non-breaking.

the split focus-streak marker classes are built only on the wrapper (`focusSheenSplit` + `sheen<Style>` + `sheen<Variant>` + force theme); the main/chevron buttons deliberately get no `focusSheen` class.

focusSheen only ever selects a hardcoded class list ([styles.focusSheenSplit, styles.sheen<Style>, styles.sheen<Variant>, force-light/force-dark]); the consumer value is never interpolated into className, so there is no class-name injection path.

the split focus-streak overlay is `inset:0` with its own border-radius and `pointer-events:none`, and the dropdown menu renders inside DropdownMenu.Portal, so the overlay cannot intercept clicks or clip the open menu.
no dangerouslySetInnerHTML / innerHTML / eval / new Function / dynamic import and no URL-from-prop usage was added; the change is one optional boolean plus CSS.
